extracted.intended_audience: AI researchers, ML practitioners, and evaluators of generative models (LLMs)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging generative model outputs across creative and technical modalities (dialogue, prose, code, images, music). Focuses on style fidelity, reasoning, multimodal synthesis, and benchmarked performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capturing the style and tone of a source author
rubrics_metrics.description: The output should capture the style and tone of the target author/genre (e.g., Plato’s dialogues) and present the intended arguments or themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: GPT-4 and ChatGPT both attempted Plato-style dialogues; evaluation judged fidelity to Plato's dialogue style. Scoring notes: look for voice, register, sentence rhythms, and whether the output presents the main arguments characteristic of the source. Anti-pattern: generic paraphrase that loses distinctive rhetorical features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dialogue for dialectical engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the dialogue format to stage a dialectical process where interlocutors question, challenge, and refine positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good outputs employ back-and-forth questioning and refinement (e.g., Socrates and interlocutor examine issues), rather than monologic exposition. GPT-4 was credited for better engaging this dialectical process. Anti-pattern: one-sided exposition or dialogue that merely reports claims without interrogation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of relevant examples and analogies
rubrics_metrics.description: Support claims with relevant, concrete examples or analogies that illuminate the argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluator should check whether examples/analogies are pertinent and clarify points (GPT-4 cited as using more relevant examples/analogies). Anti-pattern: irrelevant, misleading, or flippant examples that do not support the central claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common-sense and physical-plausibility reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate commonsense understanding of physical tasks and plausibility (e.g., proposing stable stacking of objects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposed solution is physically sensible and practical. Example: GPT-4 suggested placing book as base, arranging eggs, and precautions; ChatGPT provided a less-plausible stacking order. Scoring note: prioritize solutions that minimize obvious risks and respect basic physics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty about uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: When lacking sufficient information, the model should acknowledge uncertainty (e.g., say 'I don’t know').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good behavior: explicit admission of unknowns rather than fabricating facts. Anti-pattern: confident hallucination or inventing specifics when not supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithfulness to provided facts / no unsupported inferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrite or summarize patient/client/user-provided facts without adding information not present in the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: medical-note rewrite must only use provided facts; derived calculations (e.g., BMI) are suspect if weight not provided. Evaluation: flag claims not explicitly contained in the facts list. Scoring: deductions for adding clinical inferences, recommendations, or inferred symptoms that were not in the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to detect and report hallucinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify statements in outputs that are unsupported or fabricated relative to source data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GPT-4 can be used to identify hallucinations but is imperfect (example: it justified computing a BMI despite missing weight). Guidance: require explicit provenance checks for factual claims; prefer conservative flagging of derived claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrative / interdisciplinary synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthesize knowledge and styles across domains (e.g., literature + mathematics, programming + art) to produce coherent, creative multimodal outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete tests: produce proofs in Shakespearean style, code that generates Kandinsky-like images, or letters that merge historical persona with anachronistic content. Scoring notes: evaluate correctness in each domain, creativity of the blend, and coherence across modalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization and contextual alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctly personalize content according to the specified speaker/author, recipient, subject, and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: supporting letter by 'Mahatma Gandhi' to 'Kasturba Gandhi' for candidate 'Electron' — judge whether persona, recipient address, candidate role, and policy references are coherently aligned. Penalize generic or mismatched personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of identity when blending object and letter forms
rubrics_metrics.description: When combining letters and objects in a visual design, preserve recognizability of both the letter and the object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: pig+H, house+U, etc. Good outputs maintain identity of both components and combine them creatively. Anti-pattern: designs where one element obliterates the other or the combined image is ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Following detailed image-generation instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate images (via code or description) that match detailed textual instructions including specified objects, text elements, and scene composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: frog-in-bank scene — GPT-4 matched frog, teller, bank, and dialog text, then successfully upscaled and added requested details. Evaluate fidelity to the prompt, ability to perform iterative edits (recoloring, z-order), and completeness of requested elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatial/layout accuracy in image tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect explicit layout directives (e.g., 'blue circle on the left and red triangle on the right').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text-to-image models often fail at layout; GPT-4's code-based generation can achieve higher layout fidelity. Evaluate correct positions, relative sizes, and requested spatial relations. Penalize mismatches between described and rendered layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility as a sketch-generator for image-synthesis pipelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce structured sketches or code that can serve as a faithful intermediate input to image-synthesis models, improving adherence to instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: combining GPT-4 sketches with Stable Diffusion produced images that better followed layout and content instructions. Scoring: measure downstream fidelity improvements and alignment vs. direct text-to-image baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid musical notation and structural coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce syntactically valid music notation (ABC) with consistent time signature, coherent phrases, and repetitive/contrasting structure where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: GPT-4 produced valid ABC tunes with clear 4-bar phrases and repeats. Evaluate notation validity, meter consistency, motif structure, and phrase-level coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding and generation of harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce musically sensible harmony (chords/arpeggios) that align with the melody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed limitation: GPT-4 tended to produce adjacent-note sequences and failed to generate nontrivial harmony; references to arpeggios may be inconsistent with notes. Scoring: reward correct harmonic relationships; penalize inconsistent or musically invalid harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulation and transformation of musical structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform requested edits to musical material (e.g., invert a rising line to descending, add a bass staff) while maintaining musical compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GPT-4 successfully altered sequences and added a bass voice, though inter-voice harmony may be weak. Evaluate correctness of requested edits and resulting musical coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding proficiency under instruction and on benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce syntactically valid, semantically correct code from prompts; performance measured by benchmark metrics (HumanEval, LeetCode) such as pass@1 and pass@5 accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported metrics: GPT-4 shows substantially higher pass@k accuracies (e.g., HumanEval and curated LeetCode benchmarks). Also evaluate ability to follow problem statements exactly, handle edge cases, and produce efficient/robust solutions. Penalize syntactic errors, wrong assumptions, or solutions that fail test suites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative refinement and responsiveness to feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to follow-up corrections and error messages by refining the output (e.g., correcting proportions, adding clothing on a figure, fixing code after compiler errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: adjusting torso/arms in TikZ stick figure; improving images and 3D scenes after requests. Evaluate how well the model incorporates feedback and whether corrections preserve prior constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty beyond memorization (avoidance of simple copying)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate outputs that are not mere verbatim reproductions from training data but show inferred constructions, recombination, or genuine synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper argues evidence that the model infers novel combinations (e.g., combining letters to draw a person) rather than copying. Evaluation: check for verbatim matches to known sources and prefer creative recombinations. Caveat: always test for memorization, especially on benchmark problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-modal instruction-following ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow complex instructions that require translating textual goals into other modalities (SVG/TikZ code, 3D JS, ABC music notation), maintaining consistency across modalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: converting text prompts into SVGs, TikZ, and Javascript 3D scenes. Assess whether generated code renders to scenes matching the textual prompt and whether subsequent edit requests are handled correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative-writing craft metrics (poetic devices, meter, character contrast, specificity)
rubrics_metrics.description: For creative outputs evaluate poetic qualities (rhyme, meter), rhetorical devices (metaphor, imagery), character differentiation/contrast in dialogue, and specificity/concreteness of proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Shakespeare and Gandhi examples: GPT-4 was judged superior for rhyme/meter and for creating contrast between parties; GPT-4 used richer metaphors and concrete policy proposals in the Gandhi-letter example. Scoring rubric: A-level outputs show consistent meter/rhyme where required, strong imagery, clear role-specific voice, and concrete, specific content rather than vague generalities.
